newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee propelled higher by late rally on NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee propelled higher by late rally on NY.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures scooped further gains towards the close on active shortcovering on the strength of New York arabica futures, traders said.
"New York has been the leading light," said one trader.
By the close, most-active March contract was $32 higher at $1,265 a tonne while front-month January gained $28 at $1,331.
The remaining months were $15 to $25 up.
The rally marked the first significant rebound in prices in weeks. Traders said the market was also long overdue for a correction to an oversold condition.
The London market was called $20 higher but failed to make it by the midday close. But it gained further momentum in late afternoon as the U.S. market resumed its climb.
"We are following along with it," the trader said. "Robustas don't really have the real need to rush however we're forced to buy New York."
The New York market found support from steady commission house and trade buying but traders said there was no positive news behind the rise.

Supplies of arabica coffee were still relatively tight although a rise in exchange-certified coffee stocks, the first in weeks, served as a reminder that the flow of Latin American coffee was on the rise.
At the close of New York Monday trading, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said gradable coffee stocks grew by 2,000 60-kg bags for the week to December 6 to 2,321 bags.
In addition, 5,500 more bags were certified for delivery sometime between December 6-9, and 11,750 bag were reported pending grading in Miami warehouses.
But the fundamental picture for robusta is rather bleak on the back of a seasonal rise in supplies from the Far East and Africa. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
